headline: Cannae destroyed a Roman field army
proof: Polybius reports roughly 80,000 infantry and more than 6,000 cavalry before the battle; the defeat killed or captured much of that field army.
limits: Ancient totals are disputed and this is one field army rather than whole-war deployment.

headline: Most of the Italian alliance stayed in the war
proof: Some major communities defected but the citizen Latin-colony and allied levy system remained large enough to furnish repeated armies.
limits: Alliance durability is an institutional interpretation not a measured loyalty percentage.

headline: Rome fielded another massive war effort
proof: Taylor reconstructs roughly twenty-five legions and allied formations deployed across simultaneous theaters four years after Cannae.
limits: A modeled strategic deployment is not one field army and is not directly subtracted from the Cannae total.
